entries.proposition: Dose and schedule are stated in the Methods: 50 mg/kg daily i.p. from P5 to P21 in wild-type mice (a single dose, in 10 percent DMSO).
entries.snippet: clemastine (#1453 Tocris; 50 mg/kg solved in 10% DMSO) by intraperitoneal injections from postnatal day 5 (P5) to P21

entries.proposition: The Fig 1 legend gives the dose as micrograms per kilogram, the Results text gives milligrams and an end day of P20: three descriptions of the same schedule do not agree.
entries.snippet: Schematic representation of clemastine treatment (50 μg/kg; i.p.) during development.

entries.proposition: Dose-dependence is not tested: one dose and a vehicle arm only.
entries.snippet: we treated mice with clemastine (50 mg/kg/day, i.p.) or vehicle from postnatal day 5–20
entries.anchor: Results / Clemastine Increases the Number of Mature Oligodendrocytes

entries.proposition: Cell differentiation went up: more APC-positive mature oligodendrocytes, fewer PDGFR-positive progenitors in corpus callosum.
entries.snippet: clemastine induced a significant increase in the proportion of APC+ OLs in corpus callosum as well as in the cerebral cortex (Figure 1B).
entries.anchor: Results / Clemastine Increases the Number of Mature Oligodendrocytes

entries.proposition: Conduction velocity of myelinated callosal fibres fell, with n = 10-12 slices or animals and P below 0.01 in the text.
entries.snippet: our results revealed that action potentials transmission was significantly slower in myelinated axons (N1) of clemastine treated mice compared to control mice (Figure 2, p < 0.01, n = 10–12).

entries.proposition: The text states conduction velocity P below 0.01 while the Figure 2 legend and panel print a single asterisk (P below 0.05).
entries.snippet: (C) The input-output relationship for N1 myelinated fibers is left-shifted in clemastine-treated corpus callosum (n = 7–8). *p < 0.05.

entries.proposition: Myelinated axon number in EM fell; n = 3 mice per group.
entries.snippet: We observed that the number of myelinated axons, quantified by TEM, was reduced after clemastine treatment (Figure 4A).
entries.anchor: Results / Clemastine Administration Reduces the Number of Nodes

entries.proposition: Myelin thinning (higher g-ratio) is claimed for axons of 0-0.5 micrometre diameter only; larger axons did not differ.
entries.snippet: G-ratio analysis revealed thinner myelin sheaths in small caliber axons (0–0.5 µm) of treated animals (Figure 4B), while no differences were found in axons from 0.5 to 1 µm diameter
entries.anchor: Results / Clemastine Administration Reduces the Number of Nodes

entries.proposition: Statistical unit of the g-ratio comparison: legend gives n = 3 mice per group with 100-150 axons per group.
entries.snippet: Graphs represent the mean g-ratios for small and bigger axons (100-150 axons in control and clemastine-treated mice) and the distribution of g-ratios for control and clemastine-treated mice (n = 3 mice per group).

entries.proposition: Microglial changes: more complex morphology, lower iNOS and CD68, anti-inflammatory transcripts up, IGF and ApoE down; no change in microglial number or in myelin engulfment.
entries.snippet: Clemastine induced a massive reduction in the expression of iNOS, a proinflammatory marker, as well as the expression of the phagocytic marker CD68 (Figures 5E,F).
entries.anchor: Results / Clemastine Treatment Modifies the Expression of Activation Markers

entries.proposition: CD11c-positive microglia fell after a shorter regimen (P5 to P10) in a different mouse line; the reduction is the proposed mechanism.
entries.snippet: we treated mice with clemastine from P5 to P10. Blinded analysis showed that clemastine reduced the number of microglia CD11c+ in corpus callosum in clemastine-treated mice (Figure 6E).

entries.proposition: The authors state the myelination outcome: no increase in developmental myelination despite more oligodendrocyte differentiation.
entries.snippet: we found that developmental myelination is not increased after chronic clemastine treatment, even if clemastine induced an increase in oligodendrocyte differentiation.

entries.proposition: The authors state that blood-brain-barrier penetration was taken from an earlier study and the dose from other studies.
entries.snippet: The dose used in our study was similar to those used in other studies (30–50 mg/kg; Turski et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2016).

entries.proposition: The authors close by calling for microglia-oligodendrocyte work; the paper itself measures no behaviour, seizure or EEG endpoint.
entries.snippet: More studies are needed to understand the microglia-oligodendrocyte crosstalk necessary for myelin health maintenance.
